systems.support: Open-source software maintained by the WordPress project and community. It can be installed with many independent hosting providers.
systems.technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL or MariaDB. Browser side: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It can also provide content through its REST API.
capabilities: Large selection of themes and plugins
Built-in posts, pages, media library, users, and comments
Custom post types and page editing tools
REST API for connecting other applications
limitations: Site owners are responsible for updates, backups, hosting, and security configuration
Poorly maintained or incompatible plugins and themes can create security or stability problems
Large numbers of plugins can make a site harder to maintain

systems.support: Free, open-source CMS supported by the Drupal community, contributors, and commercial service providers.
systems.technology: Server: PHP. Databases include MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and SQLite. Browser side: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Runs on a web server such as Apache or Nginx.
capabilities: Flexible content types, fields, and content workflows
Modules and themes extend features and design
Strong user roles and permission controls
Multilingual and accessibility features
APIs and options for headless or decoupled sites
limitations: More technical knowledge is usually needed for setup and ongoing administration
Customizing complex sites can require experienced developers
Modules and major version upgrades need planning and compatibility checks

systems.support: Free, open-source CMS developed by the Joomla project and supported by its volunteer and developer community.
systems.technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL. Web server: Apache, Nginx, or Microsoft IIS. Browser side: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Templates control site layout and appearance
Extensions include components, modules, plugins, and languages
User groups and access-control levels
Built-in multilingual support and content management tools
limitations: Administrators must maintain the hosting environment and apply updates
Some advanced features require third-party extensions
Extensions and templates must be checked for compatibility during upgrades

systems.support: Commercial, hosted website builder and CMS operated by Wix. It is a subscription-based service with different plan levels.
systems.technology: Cloud-hosted SaaS platform. Wix manages the server and content storage. The site uses web technologies such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; Wix CMS provides managed content collections and APIs.
capabilities: Visual drag-and-drop site editor and ready-made templates
Managed CMS collections for structured content
Dynamic pages, forms, galleries, and connected site elements
Built-in hosting, security management, and platform updates
Business tools such as bookings and online stores
limitations: The site must run on Wix infrastructure and cannot be independently hosted elsewhere as a complete Wix site
Moving to another platform can require rebuilding parts of the site
Advanced customization is limited by the Wix platform and available plan features

sources.label: Wix site export and hosting limitation

systems.support: Commercial, hosted e-commerce platform operated by Shopify. It is offered through paid subscription plans and an app ecosystem.
systems.technology: Cloud-hosted SaaS platform. Themes use Shopify Liquid along with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Product, order, and customer data are managed by Shopify; APIs support integrations and custom storefronts.
capabilities: Product catalog, inventory, shopping cart, and checkout
Themes and theme editor for storefront design
Apps and APIs for extending store features
Payment, shipping, tax, and sales-channel integrations
Tools for managing orders and customer information
limitations: Best suited to online selling rather than every type of general-purpose website
Monthly plan and some app or transaction-related costs can add up
Advanced storefront and checkout customization can depend on plan level and platform rules
The hosted platform limits control over the underlying server and database
